1.1 Documentation Purpose

This documentation describes the complete architecture of the ABpE Portal (Automated Consultant Profile Capture System). It is intended for developers, administrators, and operators of the system and explains all components, their interaction, and configuration options.

1.2 Project Overview

The ABpE Portal is a modular, Django-based web portal for managing consultant profiles, CV extraction, email ingest, and matching processes. It is designed for operation with up to 23,000 users and scales accordingly.

Technology Stack:

  • Backend: Django 5.x, Python 3.11+
  • Database: PostgreSQL
  • Frontend: Bootstrap 5, Bootstrap Icons
  • Task Queue: Celery with RabbitMQ
  • Cache: Redis
  • Search Index: Elasticsearch

1.3 Core Architecture Principles

The architecture of the ABpE Portal follows five fundamental principles:

  • Modularity: Each functional area is an independent module with clear boundaries. Modules can be developed, tested, and deployed independently.
  • Decentralized Configuration: Each module brings its own configuration file (module.json). Central configuration is limited to system-wide settings.
  • Reusability: Global components such as CSS, JavaScript, and translations are maintained centrally and used by all modules.
  • Extensibility: Creating a new module means: create a folder, create module.json, add templates – the rest happens automatically.
  • Django Conformity: The system uses Django standards such as templates, static files, context processors, and middleware.

1.5 Data Flow Overview

The basic data flow in the system follows this pattern:

  1. User request via HTTPS → Apache/nginx → WSGI → Django
  2. Django forwards to the appropriate view (generic or specific)
  3. The view loads data from the PostgreSQL database or via API endpoints
  4. The template is rendered with the data and sent back to the client
  5. Asynchronous tasks (CV processing, email ingest) are passed to Celery via RabbitMQ
  6. Elasticsearch is used for full-text search and matching
  7. Redis serves as a cache for sessions and frequently used data
